**Finding submitted: T4C — deviation (high severity).**

**What I found**

- **Term length:** Section 8.3 (p0363) runs the Agreement to the last Receivable being paid in full or termination of the Issuer — a multi-year commitment.
- **Our exit rights:** Only cause-based. Section 7.2(a) (p0318–p0325) lists Servicer Termination Events, and Section 7.2(c) (p0327) permits removal only "[i]f a Servicer Termination Event occurs and is continuing." No at-will exit exists for the Issuer or Depositor.
- **Sections 8.1/8.2 are not a convenience right:** Optional Acquisition (p0351) requires a ≤10% pool balance and Optional Redemption (p0358) a February 2021 date plus a Make-Whole Payment, and both are Class A Certificateholder options with Administrator consent — conditional, priced, structural clean-up mechanics, not a Customer convenience termination.
- **Vendor side already exceeds preferred:** Section 7.1 (p0314) bars the Servicer from resigning at all unless legally unable to perform — stronger than either playbook level, so I mapped that element as already met and left it untouched.

**Level selection.** I targeted preferred rather than fallback deliberately: the fallback would hand the Servicer an end-of-term convenience right on 90 days' notice that Section 7.1 currently denies it, weakening us to reach a lower level. The only genuine gap is the absent Customer convenience right.

**The change.** One insertion after p0328 (new Section 7.2A) carrying only the three still-missing elements: Issuer termination for convenience, 30 days' prior written notice, and pro rata refund of prepaid Servicing Fees. The new termination is a termination "under this Agreement," so it feeds the existing Section 7.4 Successor Servicer machinery without any dangling cross-reference or collateral rewrite.
